components.note: 罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and entrapment: 罗 net, 罚 punish, 骂 scold; here a net of wrongdoing 非 catching the guilty.
非 (not, wrong) — what is wrong or unlawful; in 罪 it is the wrongdoing caught in the net.
心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恶 is a bad heart, evil.
亚 (yà) is only a loose sound hint for è.

example.hanzi: 他终于为自己的罪恶付出了代价。
example.pinyin: tā zhōngyú wèi zìjǐ de zuìè fùchū le dàijià.
example.english: He finally paid the price for his own wrongdoing.
example.fact: Dante's 'Inferno,' written in the early 14th century, organized sin into nine concentric circles of Hell ranked by severity — a literary structure so influential that it still shapes modern pop-culture depictions of moral hierarchy seven centuries later.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事讲的是善与罪恶的斗争。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi jiǎng de shì shàn yǔ zuì'è de dòuzhēng.
examples.english: This story is about the struggle between good and evil.

examples.hanzi: 战争给人类带来了很多罪恶。
examples.pinyin: Zhànzhēng gěi rénlèi dàilái le hěn duō zuì'è.
examples.english: War has brought a lot of evil to humankind.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤; water means life: 活 is alive.
舌 (shé, tongue) is a loose sound clue for huó; also in 话 huà.
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.hanzi: 今天家里的活儿都干完了。
example.pinyin: jīntiān jiā lǐ de huór dōu gàn wán le.
example.english: Today all the housework at home has been finished.
example.fact: The 40-hour workweek wasn't standardized in the US until the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938; before that, many factory laborers, including children, routinely worked 60-plus hours a week under grueling industrial-era conditions.

examples.hanzi: 他每天回家还要干很多活儿。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān huíjiā hái yào gàn hěn duō huór.
examples.english: He still has a lot of work to do when he gets home each day.

examples.hanzi: 这活儿很累，但是工资不错。
examples.pinyin: Zhè huór hěn lèi, dànshì gōngzī búcuò.
examples.english: This job is tiring, but the pay is good.

components.note: 用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 这个房间专门用来存放旧书。
example.pinyin: zhè ge fángjiān zhuānmén yònglái cúnfàng jiù shū.
example.english: This room is used specifically for storing old books.
example.fact: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault, carved into a mountainside in the Arctic, stores backup samples of over a million crop seed varieties from around the world at -18°C, in case natural disasters or war destroy the original crops.

examples.hanzi: 这把刀是用来切菜的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ dāo shì yònglái qiē cài de.
examples.english: This knife is used for cutting vegetables.

examples.hanzi: 你可以用来写字的笔在哪儿？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng lái xiězì de bǐ zài nǎr?
examples.english: Where's the pen you can write with?

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and distance, as in 过, 近, 进: 远 is a road that goes far.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuǎn; 元 also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.
辶 (walk) — movement and distance, as in 过, 近, 进: 远 is a road that goes far.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuǎn; 元 also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.

example.hanzi: 他的成绩远远超过了其他同学。
example.pinyin: tā de chéngjì yuǎnyuǎn chāoguò le qítā tóngxué.
example.english: His grades far exceeded those of his classmates.
example.fact: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, is now more than 24 billion kilometers from Earth — farther than any human-made object has ever traveled — and its radio signals still take over 22 hours to reach us.

examples.hanzi: 他远远地看见了妈妈。
examples.pinyin: Tā yuǎnyuǎn de kànjiàn le māma.
examples.english: He saw his mom from far away.

examples.hanzi: 这次的结果远远好于我的预期。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì de jiéguǒ yuǎnyuǎn hǎo yú wǒ de yùqī.
examples.english: This result is far better than I expected.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫, 吗; 哈 is the sound of laughing.
合 (hé) — near sound — 哈 is hā; 合 also sounds out 盒 hé.
禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.

example.hanzi: 电影里的哈利最终打败了敌人。
example.pinyin: diànyǐng lǐ de Hālì zuìzhōng dǎbài le dírén.
example.english: Harry in the movie eventually defeated the enemy.
example.fact: Harry Houdini performed his famous 'Chinese Water Torture Cell' escape thousands of times over a decade — submerged upside down in a locked, water-filled tank, he had roughly three minutes to escape before running out of air.

examples.hanzi: 哈利是我们班最聪明的学生。
examples.pinyin: Hālì shì wǒmen bān zuì cōngming de xuésheng.
examples.english: Harry is the smartest student in our class.

examples.hanzi: 哈利每天骑车去学校。
examples.pinyin: Hālì měitiān qí chē qù xuéxiào.
examples.english: Harry bikes to school every day.

components.note: 见 (see) — seeing and looking, as in 现, 觉, 看: 视 is to look.
礻 here is 示 (shì), the altar radical in 礼 and 神: in 视 it is the exact sound clue.

example.hanzi: 我们每天晚上看电视。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen měitiān wǎnshang kàn diànshì.
example.english: We watch TV every evening.
example.fact: 视 is a formal 'to look' that lives in compounds: 电视 (TV), 视频 (video), 近视 (nearsighted), 重视 (to take seriously), 忽视 (to overlook). Spoken Chinese uses 看 for the plain act of looking.

examples.hanzi: 他的视力不太好。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shìlì bú tài hǎo.
examples.english: His eyesight isn't very good.

examples.hanzi: 老师很重视我们的作业。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī hěn zhòngshì wǒmen de zuòyè.
examples.english: The teacher takes our homework seriously.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand; 扫 (simplified 掃) is a hand with a broom 帚, to sweep.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 描 is to draw or trace by hand.
苗 (miáo) — same sound — 描 is miáo, like 苗; 苗 also sounds out 猫 māo.

example.hanzi: 医生让他去做一次全身扫描。
example.pinyin: yīshēng ràng tā qù zuò yī cì quánshēn sǎomiáo.
example.english: The doctor had him get a full-body scan.
example.fact: The first CT scanner, built by Godfrey Hounsfield in 1971, took over five hours to scan a single brain and nearly two and a half hours to process the resulting image; modern scanners now do the equivalent in seconds.

examples.hanzi: 请用手机扫描这个二维码。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng yòng shǒujī sǎomiáo zhège èrwéimǎ.
examples.english: Please scan this QR code with your phone.

examples.hanzi: 我想把这些旧照片扫描到电脑里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ zhèxiē jiù zhàopiàn sǎomiáo dào diànnǎo lǐ.
examples.english: I want to scan these old photos into the computer.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 假 is to borrow or fake, a person lending a false front.
叚 (jiǎ) sounds like 假; also in 暇 xiá and 霞 xiá.
月 (moon, month) — time and the moon: 明 bright, 朗 clear; in 期 it is a set period, as in 星期 week.
其 (qí) is the same sound with a different tone; also in 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī.

example.hanzi: 暑假是学生们最喜欢的假期。
example.pinyin: shǔjià shì xuéshēngmen zuì xǐhuān de jiàqī.
example.english: Summer break is students' favorite vacation.
example.fact: France mandates by law that every full-time employee receive a minimum of five weeks of paid vacation annually, one of the most generous statutory minimums in the world, compared to the US, which has no federal law guaranteeing any paid vacation at all.

examples.hanzi: 春节假期我们回老家过年。
examples.pinyin: Chūnjié jiàqī wǒmen huí lǎojiā guònián.
examples.english: During the Spring Festival holiday we go back to our hometown.

examples.hanzi: 他请了一周的假期去旅行。
examples.pinyin: Tā qǐng le yì zhōu de jiàqī qù lǚxíng.
examples.english: He took a week of vacation to travel.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — heads and faces, as in 头 head, 顶 top, 额 forehead; 题 first meant forehead, then "heading".
是 (shì) gives a loose sound clue for tí; 是 also sounds out 提 tí and 堤 dī.

example.hanzi: 这道题很难。
example.pinyin: Zhè dào tí hěn nán.
example.english: This question is very hard.
example.fact: 题 counts test questions with 道: 一道题. It forms 问题 (question, problem — 没问题 means 'no problem'), 题目 (title or question) and 主题 (theme). In casual use 题 can sound like a quiz item.

examples.hanzi: 这个题目很有意思。
examples.pinyin: Zhège tímù hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: This topic is very interesting.

examples.hanzi: 你遇到什么问题了?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yùdào shénme wèntí le?
examples.english: What problem have you run into?

components.note: 缶 (clay jar) — marks pots and jars, as in 罐 jar, 缸 vat; a chipped jar is 缺, lacking.
夬 (guài/jué) is a loose hint for quē; 决 jué and 快 kuài share it.
之 (to go; foot stepping on) — the dictionary reads 乏 as a foot 之 blocked by a stroke 丿: unable to move on, so 'lacking, tired' (缺乏, 疲乏).
丿 (a left-falling stroke) — the blocking stroke on top. Memory aid: a barrier cutting across the road, so you run short.

example.hanzi: 这个地区长期缺乏干净的饮用水。
example.pinyin: zhè ge dìqū chángqí quēfá gānjìng de yǐnyòngshuǐ.
example.english: This region has long lacked clean drinking water.
example.fact: According to the WHO, roughly 2 billion people worldwide still lack access to safely managed drinking water at home, and unsafe water contributes to over 500,000 diarrheal deaths every year, disproportionately affecting children under five.

examples.hanzi: 很多孩子缺乏运动。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō háizi quēfá yùndòng.
examples.english: Many children lack exercise.

examples.hanzi: 他缺乏自信，说话声音很小。
examples.pinyin: Tā quēfá zìxìn, shuōhuà shēngyīn hěn xiǎo.
examples.english: He lacks confidence and speaks very quietly.

components.note: 义 (justice, meaning) also lends its sound to 议 yì discuss, 仪 yí ceremony and 蚁 yǐ ant — a useful clue in many characters.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 助, 努: tasks take effort. The top 夂 stands in for the traditional 務.

example.hanzi: 纳税是每个公民的义务。
example.pinyin: nàshuì shì měi gè gōngmín de yìwù.
example.english: Paying taxes is every citizen's duty.
example.fact: Switzerland still practices a form of mandatory national service, requiring most male citizens to complete military duty and remain part of a reserve into their 30s, letting the country mobilize a large trained force despite having a small standing army.

examples.hanzi: 父母有义务照顾孩子。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ yǒu yìwù zhàogù háizi.
examples.english: Parents have a duty to take care of their children.

examples.hanzi: 他每个周末都去做义务劳动。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi ge zhōumò dōu qù zuò yìwù láodòng.
examples.english: He does voluntary work every weekend.

components.note: 辶 (movement) — marks walking and roads, as in 过, 进, 送; 连 is vehicles 车 moving in a line, joined together.
车 (cart) — the vehicle in the chain, as in 转, 轮; 链 liàn (chain) is built on 连.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and connections, as in 红, 给, 经, 继; a thread that goes on.
卖 stands in for 賣 in 續, only a loose sound clue for xù.

example.hanzi: 这支球队已经连续赢了十场比赛。
example.pinyin: zhè zhī qiúduì yǐjīng liánxù yíng le shí chǎng bǐsài.
example.english: This team has won ten games in a row.
example.fact: The longest winning streak in major North American pro sports belongs to the 1971-72 Los Angeles Lakers, who won 33 consecutive NBA games — a record that has stood for over 50 years and is still considered one of the hardest in sports to break.

examples.hanzi: 这里连续下了三天雨。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ liánxù xià le sān tiān yǔ.
examples.english: It has rained here for three days in a row.

examples.hanzi: 他连续两年被评为优秀员工。
examples.pinyin: Tā liánxù liǎng nián bèi píng wéi yōuxiù yuángōng.
examples.english: He was named an outstanding employee two years in a row.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 他一时想不起那个人的名字。
example.pinyin: tā yīshí xiǎng bù qǐ nà ge rén de míngzi.
example.english: He couldn't recall that person's name for a moment.
example.fact: Short-term memory typically holds only about four to seven items at once for a matter of seconds unless they're actively rehearsed — a limit famously described in psychologist George Miller's 1956 paper 'The Magical Number Seven.'

examples.hanzi: 我一时没听懂他的意思。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yìshí méi tīng dǒng tā de yìsi.
examples.english: I didn't understand what he meant for a moment.

examples.hanzi: 他只是一时生气，别放在心上。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǐshì yìshí shēngqì, bié fàng zài xīn shàng.
examples.english: He's just angry for the moment, so don't take it to heart.

components.note: 犭 (animal; 犬 dog) — marks animals, as in 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 猪 pig; 猛 is fierce like a beast.
孟 (mèng) — close sound: 猛 měng. 孟 also sounds out 锰 měng.

example.hanzi: 他猛地推开了门。
example.pinyin: Tā měng de tuīkāi le mén.
example.english: He suddenly pushed the door open.
example.fact: 猛 can mean 'fierce' (猛兽 wild beast, 凶猛) or 'suddenly and forcefully', as in 猛地 and 猛增 ('to soar'). A fierce attack is 猛烈, and 猛 + verb adds the idea of vigour.

examples.hanzi: 这只老虎很凶猛。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī lǎohǔ hěn xiōngměng.
examples.english: This tiger is very fierce.

examples.hanzi: 风猛烈地刮着。
examples.pinyin: Fēng měngliè de guā zhe.
examples.english: The wind is blowing fiercely.

components.note: 白 (white, bright) — gives sound to 拍 pāi, 怕 pà, 伯 bó and 泊 bó. Meaning: white, clear, plain, hence "明白" understand.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.hanzi: 他白天工作,晚上上课。
example.pinyin: tā báitiān gōngzuò, wǎnshang shàngkè.
example.english: He works during the day and attends classes at night.
example.fact: North of the Arctic Circle, parts of Norway experience the Midnight Sun, where the sun doesn't set at all for up to 76 consecutive days each summer, turning 'daytime' into a continuous, round-the-clock event.

examples.hanzi: 白天太热了，我们晚上再去吧。
examples.pinyin: Báitiān tài rè le, wǒmen wǎnshang zài qù ba.
examples.english: It's too hot during the day, so let's go in the evening.

examples.hanzi: 夏天的白天比冬天长。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān de báitiān bǐ dōngtiān cháng.
examples.english: Daytime is longer in summer than in winter.

components.note: 欠 (open mouth, yawn) — marks mouths, wanting and owing, as in 歌 song, 欢 joy, 款 funds; 欲 is craving.
谷 (yù) gives the sound exactly: 欲 yù, also in 浴 yù and 裕 yù.
亡 (wáng) is a close sound clue for wàng; it also sounds out 忘 wàng (forget) and 网 wǎng.
月 (moon) — to gaze up at the moon, so to look into the distance, then to hope.

example.hanzi: 金钱无法满足他所有的欲望。
example.pinyin: jīnqián wúfǎ mǎnzú tā suǒyǒu de yùwàng.
example.english: Money can't satisfy all of his desires.
example.fact: Dopamine, often called the 'desire molecule,' spikes in the brain not at the moment of reward but during the anticipation of it — a mechanism confirmed in 1990s primate studies that helps explain why craving something can feel more intense than actually getting it.

examples.hanzi: 他没有什么物质上的欲望。
examples.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu shénme wùzhì shàng de yùwàng.
examples.english: He doesn't have many material desires.

examples.hanzi: 她有很强的学习欲望。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu hěn qiáng de xuéxí yùwàng.
examples.english: She has a strong desire to learn.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — spirits and the unseen: 魂, 魅, 愧; 魔 is a demon.
麻 (má) is a near sound match for mó; also in 磨 mó and 摩 mó.
術 (traditional) — 行 (road) plus 朮 (zhú) as sound: art, method. 术 is the sound part alone; same sound in 述 shù, as in 手术, 技术, 艺术.

example.hanzi: 他在派对上表演了一个魔术。
example.pinyin: tā zài pàiduì shàng biǎoyǎn le yī gè móshù.
example.english: He performed a magic trick at the party.
example.fact: The largest magic trick ever performed was David Copperfield's 1983 'vanishing' of the Statue of Liberty, where he made the 151-foot statue seem to disappear in front of a live audience using a rotating platform and carefully timed lighting.

examples.hanzi: 这个魔术太神奇了！
examples.pinyin: Zhège móshù tài shénqí le!
examples.english: This magic trick is amazing!

examples.hanzi: 孩子们围着魔术师看魔术。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen wéi zhe móshùshī kàn móshù.
examples.english: The children gathered around the magician to watch magic.

components.note: 辶 (movement) — marks walking and roads, as in 过, 进, 送; 连 is vehicles 车 moving in a line, joined together.
车 (cart) — the vehicle in the chain, as in 转, 轮; 链 liàn (chain) is built on 连.
王 (jade) — 王 on the left is 玉 (jade) as in 玩, 球, 现; 环 is a jade ring, as in 环境.

example.hanzi: 这是一部连环画风格的漫画。
example.pinyin: zhè shì yī bù liánhuán huà fēnggé de mànhuà.
example.english: This is a comic drawn in a serial-panel picture-book style.
example.fact: The ancient Chinese mechanical puzzle known as the Nine Linked Rings dates back over 2,000 years and requires a minimum of 341 moves to fully separate all nine interlocking rings, making it one of the earliest known combinatorial puzzles in the world.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事是连环画的形式。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi shì liánhuánhuà de xíngshì.
examples.english: This story is in the form of a picture-story book.

examples.hanzi: 警方正在调查一起连环案件。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá yì qǐ liánhuán ànjiàn.
examples.english: The police are investigating a series of linked cases.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — marks insects, as in 蜂 bee, 蚊 mosquito, 蜘 spider; 蜜 is what bees make: honey.
宓 (mì) gives the sound exactly: 蜜 mì, also in 密 mì.
虫 (insect) — marks insects, as in 蜜, 蚊, 蜘; 蜂 is a bee or wasp.
夆 (fēng) gives the sound exactly: 蜂 fēng, also in 峰 fēng and 锋 fēng.

example.hanzi: 一群蜜蜂正在花丛中采蜜。
example.pinyin: yī qún mìfēng zhèngzài huācóng zhōng cǎimì.
example.english: A swarm of bees is gathering nectar among the flowers.
example.fact: A single honeybee colony can visit up to 2 million flowers to produce just one pound of honey, and worker bees communicate the direction and distance of food sources to each other through a precise 'waggle dance.'

examples.hanzi: 蜜蜂在花丛中飞来飞去。
examples.pinyin: Mìfēng zài huācóng zhōng fēi lái fēi qù.
examples.english: Bees are flying back and forth among the flowers.

examples.hanzi: 我被一只蜜蜂蜇了一下。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bèi yì zhī mìfēng zhē le yíxià.
examples.english: I was stung by a bee.

meanings: (after a noun N and before a predicate P) the reason why N P

components.note: 之 (of, go) — oldest form is a foot leaving a starting line: "to go". Now it is a literary particle meaning "of" or "it".
斤 (axe) — cutting tools, as in 新 new and 斩 chop. 所 once echoed the sound of chopping; "place" and "that which" are later borrowed uses.
人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.

example.hanzi: 他之所以迟到,是因为路上堵车。
example.pinyin: tā zhīsuǒyǐ chídào, shì yīnwèi lùshang dǔchē.
example.english: The reason he was late is that there was traffic on the road.
example.fact: The world's longest recorded traffic jam occurred in China in August 2010 on the Beijing-Tibet Expressway, stretching roughly 100 kilometers and trapping some drivers for more than 10 days as construction and truck congestion piled up.

examples.hanzi: 我之所以喜欢这里，是因为很安静。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhīsuǒyǐ xǐhuan zhèlǐ, shì yīnwèi hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: The reason I like it here is that it's quiet.

examples.hanzi: 他之所以成功，是因为他从不放弃。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhīsuǒyǐ chénggōng, shì yīnwèi tā cóng bù fàngqì.
examples.english: The reason he succeeded is that he never gave up.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 拿; 拉 is to pull.
立 (lì) hints at the sound: 拉 lā is close, as in 垃 lā.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.
纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and ties, as in 线, 红, 约; 维 is a rope that holds things together.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) is only a loose sound clue for wéi, as in 推 tuī and 谁 shéi.
力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.

example.hanzi: 很多游客专门飞去拉斯维加斯看演出。
example.pinyin: hěn duō yóukè zhuānmén fēi qù Lāsīwéijiāsī kàn yǎnchū.
example.english: Many tourists fly specifically to Las Vegas to see shows.
example.fact: Las Vegas sits in the middle of the Mojave Desert, yet the city has become a leader in water recycling, treating and returning nearly 99% of indoor water use back to Lake Mead despite its famous fountains and pools.

examples.hanzi: 拉斯维加斯以赌场和灯光闻名。
examples.pinyin: Lāsīwéijiāsī yǐ dǔchǎng hé dēngguāng wénmíng.
examples.english: Las Vegas is famous for its casinos and lights.

examples.hanzi: 我们明年想去拉斯维加斯度假。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngnián xiǎng qù Lāsīwéijiāsī dùjià.
examples.english: We want to vacation in Las Vegas next year.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 这支球队的实力不容小觑。
example.pinyin: zhè zhī qiúduì de shílì bù róng xiǎoqiào.
example.english: This team's strength should not be underestimated.
example.fact: The US Navy's Nimitz-class aircraft carriers each displace over 100,000 tons and carry roughly 90 aircraft, giving a single ship more raw military strength than the entire air force of most countries in the world.

examples.hanzi: 他们的实力比对手强很多。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de shílì bǐ duìshǒu qiáng hěn duō.
examples.english: Their strength is much greater than their opponents'.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司的经济实力很雄厚。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī de jīngjì shílì hěn xiónghòu.
examples.english: This company has solid financial strength.

components.note: 米 (rice) — refined grain gives the idea of essence and the best part, hence 精 fine, spirit (精神).
青 (qīng) is a near sound match (-ing); the series 青 清 请 情 晴 静 helps recall jīng.
火 (fire) — the bottom part, as in 灯 lamp and 炎 flame. The dictionary lists fire as the hint: a spirit like a flickering flame, as in 灵魂.
彐 (snout) — the top part, a stroke group as in 当 and 归. 灵 simplifies 靈, so this shape is not a sound clue. Memory aid: a hand over a flame, feeling a spirit.

example.hanzi: 这部动画里有一个调皮的小精灵。
example.pinyin: zhè bù dònghuà lǐ yǒu yī gè tiáopí de xiǎo jīnglíng.
example.english: There's a mischievous little sprite in this animated show.
example.fact: Iceland's national road agency has, on occasion, rerouted actual highway construction around large boulders because of public belief in 'hidden folk,' elf-like spirits said to live inside rocks — a modern accommodation rooted in centuries-old Icelandic folklore.

examples.hanzi: 故事里的精灵住在森林深处。
examples.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ de jīnglíng zhù zài sēnlín shēnchù.
examples.english: The elf in the story lives deep in the forest.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子像个小精灵，又聪明又可爱。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi xiàng ge xiǎo jīnglíng, yòu cōngming yòu kě'ài.
examples.english: This child is like a little sprite, both smart and cute.

components.note: 阝 on the left is 阜 (steps, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: 除 first meant palace steps; to step away, remove.
余 (yú) is a loose sound clue for chú; 余 also in 涂 tú, 途 tú and 徐 xú.

example.hanzi: 除了你，大家都来了。
example.pinyin: Chúle nǐ, dàjiā dōu lái le.
example.english: Everyone came except you.
example.fact: 除 is a common word in 除了……以外 ('besides, except'). It also means 'divide' in math (除法, 6除以2 is 6 divided by 2) and gives 除夕 (New Year's Eve), the night that 'removes' the old year.

examples.hanzi: 请把这个文件从电脑里删除。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhège wénjiàn cóng diànnǎo li shānchú.
examples.english: Please delete this file from the computer.

examples.hanzi: 十除以二等于五。
examples.pinyin: Shí chú yǐ èr děngyú wǔ.
examples.english: Ten divided by two is five.

components.note: 大 (big) — marks size and swagger, as in 太 too, 夺; 夸 is to make something sound big, to boast.
亏 (kuī) hints at the sound: 夸 kuā is close to 垮 kuǎ and 跨 kuà.
弓 (bow) — bows and stretching, as in 弯 bend, 弹 pluck, 引 draw: 张 is to draw a bow.
长 (zhǎng) is a close sound clue for zhāng.

example.hanzi: 他说话总是有点夸张。
example.pinyin: tā shuōhuà zǒng shì yǒudiǎn kuāzhāng.
example.english: He always exaggerates a bit when he talks.
example.fact: American folktales about Paul Bunyan, a giant lumberjack supposedly responsible for carving the Grand Canyon by dragging his axe, are a well-documented example of the 19th-century 'tall tale' tradition, built entirely on outlandish exaggeration for entertainment.

examples.hanzi: 你说得太夸张了吧？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de tài kuāzhāng le ba?
examples.english: Aren't you exaggerating?

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服的设计有点夸张。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu de shèjì yǒudiǎn kuāzhāng.
examples.english: The design of this garment is a bit over the top.

components.note: 夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding the reins.
空 (kōng) is a close sound clue for kòng; 空 also in 腔 qiāng and 孔 kǒng.

example.hanzi: 汽车在冰面上突然失控打滑。
example.pinyin: qìchē zài bīngmiàn shàng tūrán shīkòng dǎhuá.
example.english: The car suddenly went out of control and skidded on the ice.
example.fact: The Chernobyl nuclear disaster of 1986 began when a routine safety test went out of control during a power surge, causing reactor 4 to explode; the resulting radioactive fallout was detected across most of Europe within days.

examples.hanzi: 刹车坏了，车子失控了。
examples.pinyin: Shāchē huài le, chēzi shīkòng le.
examples.english: The brakes broke and the car went out of control.

examples.hanzi: 他一生气，情绪就失控了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yì shēngqì, qíngxù jiù shīkòng le.
examples.english: When he gets angry, his emotions go out of control.

components.note: 木 (wood) — wood radical — tables are wooden furniture, like 椅 chair, 板 board.
卓 (zhuō) — same sound as 桌 zhuō — a clear sound clue.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 钥匙就放在桌上,你没看到吗?
example.pinyin: yàoshi jiù fàng zài zhuōshàng, nǐ méi kàndào ma?
example.english: The keys are right there on the table — didn't you see them?
example.fact: Formal dining etiquette around the table varies widely — in the UK, placing elbows on the table is traditionally considered rude, while in France it's commonly accepted and even expected during conversation between courses.

examples.hanzi: 你的手机在桌上。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shǒujī zài zhuōshàng.
examples.english: Your phone is on the table.

examples.hanzi: 桌上放着一杯热茶。
examples.pinyin: Zhuōshàng fàng zhe yì bēi rè chá.
examples.english: There is a cup of hot tea on the table.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
千 (thousand) — 千 is a number built on the old form of 人 with an extra stroke; its sound is also in 迁 qiān.

example.hanzi: 这幅画拍卖出了一千多美元。
example.pinyin: zhè fú huà pāimài chū le yīqiān duō měiyuán.
example.english: This painting sold at auction for more than a thousand dollars.
example.fact: The Japanese tradition of folding 1,000 paper cranes, senbazuru, is believed to grant a wish and was popularized worldwide after Sadako Sasaki, a survivor of the Hiroshima bombing, attempted to fold 1,000 cranes before her death from leukemia in 1955.

examples.hanzi: 这个手机要一千块钱。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shǒujī yào yì qiān kuài qián.
examples.english: This phone costs a thousand yuan.

examples.hanzi: 这座山有一千多米高。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò shān yǒu yìqiān duō mǐ gāo.
examples.english: This mountain is over a thousand meters high.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is the money radical — 财, 贵, 买, 费; betting stakes money.
者 (zhě) — near hint — 赌 is dǔ; 者 also sounds out 堵 dǔ and 都 dū.
十 (ten) — complete and wide: 博 is broad, abundant.
尃 (fū) is a loose sound clue for bó; 尃 also in 搏 bó, 薄 báo and 缚 fù.

example.hanzi: 长期赌博让他欠下了巨额债务。
example.pinyin: chángqí dǔbó ràng tā qiàn xià le jù'é zhàiwù.
example.english: Long-term gambling left him deeply in debt.
example.fact: The oldest known dice, carved from bone, date back roughly 5,000 years to sites in Iran, showing that games of chance and gambling-like behavior are among the oldest recorded human pastimes, predating written history in many cultures.

examples.hanzi: 赌博会让人倾家荡产。
examples.pinyin: Dǔbó huì ràng rén qīngjiādàngchǎn.
examples.english: Gambling can leave a person penniless.

examples.hanzi: 他后悔自己曾经赌博。
examples.pinyin: Tā hòuhuǐ zìjǐ céngjīng dǔbó.
examples.english: He regrets having gambled.

components.note: 夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.
土 (earth) — 土 is earth and land, as in 地, 城, 块; 境 is a stretch of land, a border or condition.
竟 (jìng) — same sound — 境 is jìng, like 竟; 竟 also sounds out 镜 jìng.

example.hanzi: 公司目前的处境十分艰难。
example.pinyin: gōngsī mùqián de chǔjìng shífēn jiānnán.
example.english: The company's current situation is very difficult.
example.fact: Ernest Shackleton's 1915 Antarctic expedition became one of history's most famous survival situations when their ship Endurance was crushed by pack ice; all 28 crew members nonetheless survived over a year stranded on ice and in open boats before a daring rescue.

examples.hanzi: 我很理解你现在的处境。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn lǐjiě nǐ xiànzài de chǔjìng.
examples.english: I understand your situation right now.

examples.hanzi: 他在那个国家的处境很危险。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài nàge guójiā de chǔjìng hěn wēixiǎn.
examples.english: His situation in that country is very dangerous.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and worship: 神 god, 祝 wish, 福 fortune; 礼 are ritual courtesies.
月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.

example.hanzi: 他们要求客人穿礼服出席晚宴。
example.pinyin: Tāmen yāoqiú kèrén chuān lǐfú chūxí wǎnyàn.
example.english: They required guests to wear formal attire to the dinner.
example.fact: The modern tuxedo traces to an 1886 dinner at Tuxedo Park, New York, where a young socialite's shortened black dinner jacket — modeled on a style popularized by the future King Edward VII — broke from the era's mandatory tailcoat. The abbreviated jacket caught on and became the informal blueprint for men's formal wear ever since.

examples.hanzi: 她的婚礼上穿了一件白色礼服。
examples.pinyin: Tā de hūnlǐ shàng chuān le yí jiàn báisè lǐfú.
examples.english: She wore a white gown at her wedding.

examples.hanzi: 我想租一套礼服去参加毕业典礼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zū yí tào lǐfú qù cānjiā bìyè diǎnlǐ.
examples.english: I want to rent a formal outfit for the graduation ceremony.

components.note: 臣 (eye) — 臣 is a picture of an eye looking down; with a person leaning, 卧 is lying down.
广 (shelter) — buildings, as in 店 shop, 床 bed, 度 degree; 底 is the base of a house.
氐 (dī) is a close sound clue for dǐ; also in 低 dī and 抵 dǐ.

example.hanzi: 警方派了一名卧底去调查那个犯罪团伙。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng pàile yī míng wòdǐ qù diàochá nàge fànzuì tuánhuǒ.
example.english: The police sent an undercover agent to investigate that criminal gang.
example.fact: FBI agent Joseph Pistone spent six years undercover inside the Bonanno crime family under the alias 'Donnie Brasco,' gathering evidence that led to more than 100 convictions. It remains one of the longest sustained undercover infiltrations in U.S. law-enforcement history.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影讲的是一个警察去黑帮卧底的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎng de shì yí gè jǐngchá qù hēibāng wòdǐ de gùshi.
examples.english: This film is about a policeman who goes undercover in a gang.

examples.hanzi: 原来公司里有一个卧底，一直在给对手传消息。
examples.pinyin: Yuánlái gōngsī lǐ yǒu yí gè wòdǐ, yìzhí zài gěi duìshǒu chuán xiāoxi.
examples.english: It turns out there was a mole in the company, passing information to the rival all along.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — scattered raindrops, hence small bits and nothing; also in 雪 snow, 雷 thunder.
令 (lìng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 铃 líng, 龄 líng and 领 lǐng.

example.hanzi: 今天早上的气温是零度。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān zǎoshang de qìwēn shì líng dù.
example.english: This morning's temperature is zero degrees.
example.fact: 零 is zero (not the older 〇, though both are used), and it also fills gaps in numbers: 一百零五 is 105, and 三千零二十 is 3,020. It also means 'odd, scattered', as in 零钱 (small change) and 零食 (snacks).

examples.hanzi: 现在是零下五度。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài shì língxià wǔ dù.
examples.english: It's five degrees below zero now.

examples.hanzi: 孩子喜欢吃零食。
examples.pinyin: Háizi xǐhuan chī língshí.
examples.english: Kids like to eat snacks.

meanings: special collection of printed or broadcast material

components.note: 专 (zhuān) also gives its sound to 转 zhuǎn, 传 chuán, 砖 zhuān and 团 tuán (traditional 專).
车 (cart, vehicle) — marks wheeled things, as in 转, 轮, 较; 辑 originally meant carriage parts, then gathering and editing.

example.hanzi: 这位歌手的新专辑上市后立刻登上排行榜冠军。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi gēshǒu de xīn zhuānjí shàngshì hòu lìkè dēngshàng páihángbǎng guànjūn.
example.english: This singer's new album shot to the top of the charts as soon as it was released.
example.fact: Michael Jackson's 1982 album Thriller remains the best-selling album of all time worldwide, with estimated sales exceeding 70 million copies. It was also the first album to send seven of its nine tracks into the U.S. Top 10 singles chart.

examples.hanzi: 我最喜欢她第二张专辑里的那首歌。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan tā dì-èr zhāng zhuānjí lǐ de nà shǒu gē.
examples.english: My favorite is the song on her second album.

examples.hanzi: 这本杂志出了一期旅行专辑。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn zázhì chū le yì qī lǚxíng zhuānjí.
examples.english: This magazine put out a special travel issue.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
子 (child) — children and offspring: 孩 child, 学 study, 孙 grandchild; 存 means to keep or survive.
才 (cái) is only a loose sound hint for cún.

example.hanzi: 请记得随时保存你的工作文件，以免数据丢失。
example.pinyin: Qǐng jìde suíshí bǎocún nǐ de gōngzuò wénjiàn, yǐmiǎn shùjù diūshī.
example.english: Please remember to save your work files regularly so you don't lose any data.
example.fact: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault, built into a mountainside on a Norwegian Arctic island, preserves over a million seed samples at -18°C as a backup against the loss of crop diversity. Its remote, cold, geologically stable location was chosen specifically so the seeds could survive power failures, war, or climate disasters.

examples.hanzi: 这些老照片保存得很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē lǎo zhàopiàn bǎocún de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: These old photos have been very well preserved.

examples.hanzi: 牛奶要放在冰箱里保存。
examples.pinyin: Niúnǎi yào fàng zài bīngxiāng lǐ bǎocún.
examples.english: Milk should be kept in the fridge.

components.note: 彡 (decorative strokes) — marks patterns and adornment, as in 形 shape, 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 修 is to tidy and decorate, then repair.
攸 (yōu) is only a loose hint for xiū; 悠 yōu shares it.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.hanzi: 两国领导人会面，试图修好长期紧张的关系。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó lǐngdǎorén huìmiàn, shìtú xiūhǎo chángqí jǐnzhāng de guānxì.
example.english: The leaders of the two countries met, trying to mend their long-strained relationship.
example.fact: In 1972, U.S. President Richard Nixon's visit to China ended more than two decades of diplomatic isolation between the two nations. The trip was so unexpected at the time that it gave rise to the phrase 'a Nixon goes to China,' now used to describe any leader making a surprising political reversal.

examples.hanzi: 师傅，我的自行车能修好吗？
examples.pinyin: Shīfu, wǒ de zìxíngchē néng xiūhǎo ma?
examples.english: Mister, can you fix my bike?

examples.hanzi: 爸爸花了一个下午才把水龙头修好。
examples.pinyin: Bàba huā le yí gè xiàwǔ cái bǎ shuǐlóngtóu xiūhǎo.
examples.english: It took Dad a whole afternoon to get the faucet fixed.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.
力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.

example.hanzi: 她的故事深深地感动了在场的每一个人。
example.pinyin: Tā de gùshì shēnshēn de gǎndòngle zàichǎng de měi yī gèrén.
example.english: Her story deeply moved everyone present.
example.fact: Emotional tears carry a different chemical makeup than tears triggered by irritants like onions — they contain stress hormones and natural painkillers called leucine-enkephalins. That difference is part of why crying from strong emotion can leave people feeling physically calmer afterward.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影太感动了，我看哭了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng tài gǎndòng le, wǒ kàn kū le.
examples.english: This movie was so moving that I cried.

examples.hanzi: 朋友们送的生日礼物让我很感动。
examples.pinyin: Péngyoumen sòng de shēngrì lǐwù ràng wǒ hěn gǎndòng.
examples.english: The birthday gift my friends gave me touched me deeply.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and connections, as in 红, 给, 经, 系; 继 is to keep a thread going.
手 (hand) — the hand family: 打, 拿, 拉. 承 is usually explained as hands lifting something, to bear or accept (承认 admit, 承诺 promise).

example.hanzi: 他继承了父亲的公司和全部财产。
example.pinyin: Tā jìchéngle fùqīn de gōngsī hé quánbù cáichǎn.
example.english: He inherited his father's company and all his assets.
example.fact: Mitochondrial DNA is passed down almost exclusively through the maternal line, since sperm mitochondria are typically destroyed after fertilization. That property lets scientists trace maternal ancestry back tens of thousands of years through a method called mitochondrial DNA analysis.

examples.hanzi: 他想继承爷爷留下的小饭馆。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng jìchéng yéye liú xià de xiǎo fànguǎn.
examples.english: He wants to take over the little restaurant his grandfather left behind.

examples.hanzi: 我们应该继承和发扬这些优良传统。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi jìchéng hé fāyáng zhèxiē yōuliáng chuántǒng.
examples.english: We should carry on and promote these fine traditions.

components.note: 日 (sun) — marks sun, daylight and time, as in 明 bright, 晚 evening, 早 early; 晃 is bright, dazzling light, then shaking light, as in 晃动 sway.
光 (light) — sun 日 over light 光: dazzling brightness.

example.hanzi: 船在水上晃来晃去。
example.pinyin: Chuán zài shuǐ shàng huàng lái huàng qù.
example.english: The boat sways back and forth on the water.
example.fact: 晃 has two readings: huàng means 'to shake, sway' (摇晃, 晃动), while huǎng means 'to dazzle' or 'flash past', as in 一晃 ('in a flash') and 晃眼. 晃来晃去 is a pattern, 'swaying back and forth'.

examples.hanzi: 别晃桌子,水要洒了。
examples.pinyin: Bié huàng zhuōzi, shuǐ yào sǎ le.
examples.english: Don't shake the table; the water will spill.

examples.hanzi: 他在街上晃了一下午。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jiē shang huàng le yí xiàwǔ.
examples.english: He wandered around the streets all afternoon.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family terms, as in 妈 mom, 好 good, 姐 sister; 女 (nǚ) also loosely echoes the rú sound.
口 (mouth) — speech; 如 originally meant "to follow, accord with", later "as, like"; also in 汝 rǔ and 茹 rú.
今 (now, today) — gives sound to 琴 qín, 含 hán, 念 niàn and 吟 yín; the old picture is uncertain.

example.hanzi: 如今很多人都习惯用手机支付。
example.pinyin: Rújīn hěn duō rén dōu xíguàn yòng shǒujī zhīfù.
example.english: Nowadays, many people are used to paying with their phones.
example.fact: China's mobile payment volume surpassed $50 trillion in transactions annually by the early 2020s, driven largely by QR-code systems like Alipay and WeChat Pay that let even street vendors accept payments without ever installing a card reader.

examples.hanzi: 这个小镇如今已经变成了大城市。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎo zhèn rújīn yǐjīng biànchéng le dà chéngshì.
examples.english: This small town has now become a big city.

examples.hanzi: 他以前很瘦，如今却胖了不少。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐqián hěn shòu, rújīn què pàng le bù shǎo.
examples.english: He used to be thin, but now he has put on quite a bit of weight.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.

example.hanzi: 孩子们放学后喜欢在公园打球。
example.pinyin: Háizimen fàngxué hòu xǐhuan zài gōngyuán dǎqiú.
example.english: The kids like playing ball in the park after school.
example.fact: Basketball was invented in December 1891 by Canadian physical education instructor James Naismith, who nailed two peach baskets to a gymnasium balcony in Springfield, Massachusetts, to give restless students an indoor game to play during the winter.

examples.hanzi: 周末你想不想和我们一起打球？
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò nǐ xiǎng bu xiǎng hé wǒmen yìqǐ dǎqiú?
examples.english: Do you want to play ball with us this weekend?

examples.hanzi: 他每天早上都去操场打球。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi tiān zǎoshang dōu qù cāochǎng dǎqiú.
examples.english: He goes to the sports field to play ball every morning.

components.note: 礻 (spirit, from 示) — marks ritual and spirits, as in 神 god, 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; 祖 is an ancestor, honoured at the altar.
且 (qiě) hints at the sound: 祖 zǔ is close to 组 zǔ, 阻 zǔ and 租 zū.
母 (mother) — a woman 女 with two dots for breasts: a nursing mother. 母 also appears in 每 měi, 海 hǎi and 梅 méi.

example.hanzi: 我祖母今年八十岁了，身体还很健康。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zǔmǔ jīnnián bāshí suì le, shēntǐ hái hěn jiànkāng.
example.english: My grandmother is eighty years old this year and still in good health.
example.fact: The verified oldest person in recorded history, Jeanne Calment of France, lived to 122 years and 164 days, outliving her own daughter and grandchildren. She reportedly took up fencing at 85 and still rode a bicycle at 100.

examples.hanzi: 祖母给我讲了很多小时候的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zǔmǔ gěi wǒ jiǎng le hěn duō xiǎo shíhou de gùshi.
examples.english: My grandmother told me many stories from my childhood.

examples.hanzi: 每年春节，我们都回乡下看望祖母。
examples.pinyin: Měi nián Chūnjié, wǒmen dōu huí xiāngxia kànwàng zǔmǔ.
examples.english: Every Spring Festival we go back to the countryside to visit Grandma.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
父 (father) — marks the father, as in 爸 dad, 爷 grandfather; 爹 is dad.
多 (duō) is only a loose hint for diē.

example.hanzi: 村里的孩子们都亲切地叫他老爹。
example.pinyin: Cūn lǐ de háizimen dōu qīnqiè de jiào tā lǎodiē.
example.english: The children in the village all affectionately call him 'old man.'
example.fact: In many rural Chinese dialects, kinship terms like 'lǎodiē' extend beyond blood relatives to any respected elder man in the community, reflecting a broader East Asian custom of using family titles as a mark of social respect rather than a literal relation.

examples.hanzi: 我老爹年轻时是个木匠。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ lǎodiē niánqīng shí shì gè mùjiang.
examples.english: My old man was a carpenter when he was young.

examples.hanzi: 老爹，您慢点儿走，小心台阶。
examples.pinyin: Lǎodiē, nín màn diǎnr zǒu, xiǎoxīn táijiē.
examples.english: Take it slow, old sir, and watch the steps.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water — dyeing means soaking in a liquid.
木 (tree, plant) — 木 is the plant dye material, steeped in water to make colour.

example.hanzi: 她把头发染成了棕色。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ tóufa rǎn chéng le zōngsè.
example.english: She dyed her hair brown.
example.fact: 染 means to dye or to colour (染发), and also to be infected or tainted: 感染 (infect), 传染 (spread, be contagious) and 污染 (pollute).

examples.hanzi: 她去美发店染头发。
examples.pinyin: Tā qù měifàdiàn rǎn tóufa.
examples.english: She goes to the hair salon to dye her hair.

examples.hanzi: 他被朋友传染了感冒。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi péngyou chuánrǎn le gǎnmào.
examples.english: He caught a cold from a friend.

components.note: 止 (foot) — a person 人 standing on tiptoe 止 to see farther; hence to aspire or plan (企图), also 企业 enterprise.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries and surroundings: 国 country, 园 garden, 回 return; 图 is a drawn plan of a region.

example.hanzi: 警方挫败了那名罪犯企图逃跑的计划。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng cuòbàile nà míng zuìfàn qǐtú táopǎo de jìhuà.
example.english: The police foiled the criminal's attempt to escape.
example.fact: Alcatraz, the maximum-security island prison in San Francisco Bay, recorded 14 separate escape attempts involving 36 inmates during its 29 years of operation. Officially none succeeded, though the fate of three men who vanished during a 1962 attempt has never been conclusively determined.

examples.hanzi: 他企图蒙混过关，结果被老师发现了。
examples.pinyin: Tā qǐtú ménghùn guòguān, jiéguǒ bèi lǎoshī fāxiàn le.
examples.english: He tried to get away with it, but the teacher noticed.

examples.hanzi: 小偷企图从窗户爬进屋里。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎotōu qǐtú cóng chuānghu pá jìn wū lǐ.
examples.english: The thief tried to climb into the house through the window.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
女 (woman) — women and family terms, as in 妈 mom, 好 good, 姐 sister; 女 (nǚ) also loosely echoes the rú sound.
口 (mouth) — speech; 如 originally meant "to follow, accord with", later "as, like"; also in 汝 rǔ and 茹 rú.

example.hanzi: 与其抱怨，不如想办法解决问题。
example.pinyin: Yǔqí bàoyuàn, bùrú xiǎng bànfǎ jiějué wèntí.
example.english: Rather than complain, it would be better to find a way to solve the problem.
example.fact: Psychologist Barry Schwartz's research on the 'paradox of choice' found that people offered fewer options often report greater satisfaction with their final decision than those given many alternatives, because excess choice increases regret and the sense that a better option was missed.

examples.hanzi: 我的中文不如你好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de Zhōngwén bùrú nǐ hǎo.
examples.english: My Chinese is not as good as yours.

examples.hanzi: 天气这么热，不如我们去游泳吧。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì zhème rè, bùrú wǒmen qù yóuyǒng ba.
examples.english: It's so hot; we might as well go swimming.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — bird element as in 难, 谁, 集; in 雇 it is historical, so just treat it as a part.
户 (hù) — sounds out 雇 gù — close (same final, h→g); 户 also sounds out 顾 gù, so 雇 and 顾 sound alike.
亻 (person) — marks people, as in 你, 他, 做; 佣 is a hired person.
用 (yòng) gives the sound: 佣 yōng is close, and 用 also means use.

example.hanzi: 这家公司雇佣了两百多名员工。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī gùyōngle liǎng bǎi duō míng yuángōng.
example.english: This company employs more than two hundred staff.
example.fact: The eight-hour workday, now standard across much of the world, grew out of the 19th-century labor slogan 'eight hours for work, eight hours for rest, eight hours for what we will,' first widely championed during the 1886 general strikes in the United States that also gave rise to May Day.

examples.hanzi: 老板打算再雇佣两个新人。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn dǎsuàn zài gùyōng liǎng gè xīnrén.
examples.english: The boss plans to hire two more new people.

examples.hanzi: 他们雇佣了一位会说英语的导游。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen gùyōng le yí wèi huì shuō Yīngyǔ de dǎoyóu.
examples.english: They hired a tour guide who speaks English.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
阝 on the left is 阜 (mound, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: a steep place, a risky pass.
佥 (qiān) is a loose sound clue for xiǎn; 佥 also in 检 jiǎn, 剑 jiàn, 脸 liǎn and 验 yàn.
⺮ (bamboo) — 竹 (bamboo) as in 笔, 筷, 篮; boxes and baskets were woven from bamboo, so 箱 is a box or chest.
相 (xiāng) — same sound — 箱 is xiāng, just like 相.

example.hanzi: 他把重要文件都锁在保险箱里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhòngyào wénjiàn dōu suǒ zài bǎoxiǎnxiāng lǐ.
example.english: He locked all the important documents in the safe.
example.fact: The vault at Fort Knox, the U.S. Bullion Depository, is protected by a door weighing more than 20 tons and set behind granite walls and steel-lined concrete. Despite its legendary reputation, the facility has never actually been robbed.

examples.hanzi: 酒店房间里有一个小保险箱。
examples.pinyin: Jiǔdiàn fángjiān lǐ yǒu yí gè xiǎo bǎoxiǎnxiāng.
examples.english: There is a small safe in the hotel room.

examples.hanzi: 我忘了保险箱的密码。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wàng le bǎoxiǎnxiāng de mìmǎ.
examples.english: I forgot the combination of the safe.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks walls and slopes, as in 院, 阶, 附; 隔 is to separate with a partition.
鬲 (gé) gives the sound exactly: 隔 gé.
離 (traditional) — 隹 (bird) plus 离 as sound (lí). 离 was an old name for a mythical beast, so the 'leave' sense comes from 離; 离 kept only the sound part.

example.hanzi: 医院把患有传染病的病人隔离起来。
example.pinyin: Yīyuàn bǎ huàn yǒu chuánrǎnbìng de bìngrén gélí qǐlái.
example.english: The hospital isolated patients with the contagious disease.
example.fact: The word quarantine originates from the Venetian practice, starting in the 14th century, of holding ships arriving from plague-affected ports offshore for 'quaranta giorni' — forty days — before allowing passengers and cargo to land.

examples.hanzi: 他从国外回来后要隔离两个星期。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng guówài huílái hòu yào gélí liǎng gè xīngqī.
examples.english: After returning from abroad he has to isolate for two weeks.

examples.hanzi: 这堵墙把噪音隔离在外面。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dǔ qiáng bǎ zàoyīn gélí zài wàimiàn.
examples.english: This wall keeps the noise out.

components.note: 西 (west) — traditionally a bird settling on its nest at sunset, hence west; 西 turns up in 要 and 栖.
衣 (clothing) — clothes and wear: 衬, 被, 袋; 装 is dress, then to pretend or to load.
壮 (zhuàng) is a near sound match for zhuāng; also in 状 zhuàng and 妆 zhuāng.

example.hanzi: 他第一次穿西装去参加面试。
example.pinyin: Tā dì yī cì chuān xīzhuāng qù cānjiā miànshì.
example.english: He wore a suit for the first time to go to a job interview.
example.fact: The modern business suit descends from a 17th-century English fashion reform pushed by King Charles II, who in 1666 decreed a simpler coat, waistcoat, and breeches as court dress to distance England from ornate French styles — a look that gradually evolved into today's suit.

examples.hanzi: 爸爸上班的时候总是穿西装。
examples.pinyin: Bàba shàngbān de shíhou zǒngshì chuān xīzhuāng.
examples.english: Dad always wears a suit when he goes to work.

examples.hanzi: 这套西装是我上个月新买的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tào xīzhuāng shì wǒ shàng gè yuè xīn mǎi de.
examples.english: I bought this suit new last month.
